featured_reviews.name: Vishwesh Ranadive
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Highly Disappointing Maharashtrian Food
Overall Rating: 3/10 (Based primarily on food Taste and facilities)
My recent visit to Vinay in Girgaon was a profound disappointment, particularly for anyone seeking authentic, high-quality Maharashtrian snacks. The experience was marred by poor execution of core dishes and subpar facilities, resulting in one of the worst quick-service dining experiences I've had in a while.
The Food Verdict
The most critical failure of the visit was the Misal Pav.
• Misal Pav: 1/10
This was, quite frankly, one of the worst Misal Pavs I have ever encountered. It lacked the characteristic spice, texture, and authentic flavor profile that defines this Maharashtrian staple. It was sweet 😂. If Misal is your purpose for visiting, please look elsewhere.
• Other Dishes: 3/10 (Okish)
We also sampled the Sabudana Wada, Vatana Pattice, and Veg Biryani. While these items were merely "okish," they still scored a very low 3 out of 10. They lacked freshness, or any distinguishing quality to warrant a recommendation or even a second thought.
Ambiance and Facilities
On a positive note, the restaurant offers good sitting options, including both AC and Non-AC sections, which is a rare plus point in this category.
However, the facility challenges are severe:
• Parking: There is no dedicated parking available, which can be a significant hassle in the congested Girgaon area.
• Toilets: The washroom facilities were, without exaggeration, the worst. This is a major area needing immediate attention and upkeep.
Final Recommendation
If your goal is to experience good, authentic, and delicious Maharashtrian cuisine, do not visit Vinay. You will be better served by traveling a little further to established names.
Alternative Recommendations for Authentic Maharashtrian Food:
• Misal Pav: For a truly great Misal, visit Mamledar Misal (Thane).
• General Maharashtrian Cuisine: For excellent, reliable snacks and meals, Prakash Shuddh Upahar Kendra (Dadar) remains a gold standard.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this restaurant on the way to Crawford Market. I’ve been coming here since childhood—not very regularly, but occasionally.I went for kheema pav, but the owner suggested bheja along with kheema pav, so I went with his recommendation.

When the dish arrived, the portion size was quite small and didn’t feel worth ₹240. On top of that, they charge ₹20 extra for pav, which feels a bit excessive. The taste was very good—rich and flavorful—but slightly too spicy and oily for my liking.

In the afternoon, the place is usually packed, especially for non-vegetarian dishes. However, as a local Mumbaikar, I do feel the pricing is on the higher side. Either the cost should be more reasonable or the portion size should be increased to justify it.

The owner was actively moving around, asking customers for feedback and promoting items like fish fry, caramel custard, and solkadhi. While this does help in building customer relationships, a major drawback comes at the time of billing—they do not accept UPI payments, only cash.

featured_reviews.name: Curious Fork
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Feast Worth the Journey from Pune!
We travelled all the way from Pune just to eat at Hotel Grant House, and it was worth every minute. This restaurant has been on our bucket list for a while, and it thoroughly satisfied our hunger. We left full and sent them a lot of blessings for such delicious food!  We were hungry so didn't have the patience to take pictures to post.
The Fried Bombil, Crab Lollipop, Prawns Masala, and Prawns Pulav were outstanding. The river prawns were sweet and cooked perfectly.Mutton Khima was flavourful, well-spiced, and delicious. Their last portion of caramel custard had our name on it, so glad! That was so good too.
The staff is incredibly polite and attentive. A special thanks to the manager, Shridhar, who suggested a few items every single recommendation was spot on and scrumptious.
The restaurant is located in a crowded area and the street is not well lit but the food is so good that the surroundings do not matter. It is a definitive must-try place if you are in the area. We only wish they had a branch in Pune!

Food Review: A Major Disappointment
​I truly believe one shouldn't speak ill of food, but I had an absolutely terrible experience here.
​We ordered the Prawns Koliwada and Crispy Chicken. Given the massive hype surrounding this restaurant, we expected the food to be exceptional. As a seafood lover—especially prawns fry—I was genuinely shocked from the very first bite. The Prawns Koliwada was completely tasteless; the spice profile was missing and there was no salt at all.
​To make matters worse, when my wife cut into a prawn, we realized they hadn't been cleaned properly. The digestive tracks (veins) were still inside. Every single prawn was like that, which completely ruined our appetite. On top of that, the dish was incredibly expensive.

​The Crispy Chicken
​The second dish was just as bad. It was so sour that after just one bite, we had to ask the waiter to pack it up. Neither my wife nor my kids could eat it—it was a total waste of money. I’ve had Crispy Chicken at many places, but this was the worst. Honestly, the local Chinese joint in my neighborhood makes it better.

​The Lesson Learned
​This experience taught me one thing: don't just rush to a restaurant based on an influencer's video. You have to check real reviews first. I have no idea what people actually like about the food there. My wife and I are beyond disappointed.

Secondly, i found it expensive based on where we ate and what we ate.

featured_reviews.review_text:

Each dish can have different flavours. The Prawn rava fry and the Surmai fry both were lovely. The Prawn curry was a bit sweetish. The vades were the best. They really need to improve on the veg food. He suggested Dry paneer chilly along with Ghavan like Neer dosa which was weird to have without gravy. For the main course I specifically asked if the drumstick dish was a curry since I wanted to have with rice. He said yes and then a dry dish came up. They really need to improve their service. It took forever to get simple dishes. Waiting for food was almost half hour or more .
Also found the price a bit steep
Btw- for those who don’t know Poco Loco and Konkani Haven in chowpatty is in the same restaurant.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Golden Chimney offered a comfortable and enjoyable dining experience during our visit.

The ambience inside the restaurant was quite good, especially after entering from the outside summer heat into the air-conditioned seating area.

There happened to be an IPL match playing during the visit as well, which added a lively atmosphere without making the place feel too noisy or chaotic.

For drinks, I ordered a fresh lime water, which was refreshing and suited the weather well.

For starters, we ordered the Murgh Lasoni Tikka and Classic Chicken Chilly. Both dishes were enjoyable, though the Murgh Lasoni Tikka stood out more for its flavour and preparation.

For the mains, we had the Butter Chicken, which was well prepared and satisfying.

Service was good, seating was comfortable, and overall the restaurant provided a pleasant dine-in experience.

All in all, a good restaurant option in the Opera House / Lamington Road area for a relaxed lunch or dinner with decent food and ambience.

featured_reviews.name: Anmol Sanyasi
featured_reviews.review_text:
From the very first meal, Golden Chimney completely won us over. The food is absolutely delicious — every dish is rich in flavor, beautifully balanced, and full of authentic taste. You can truly taste Mumbai in the food — the spices, the freshness, and the variety all come together perfectly. Each bite felt thoughtfully prepared and full of character.
What made our experience even more special was the staff. They are incredibly gentle, kind, and genuinely thoughtful. The hospitality here stands out. They pay attention to every detail and make sure you feel comfortable and taken care of. Whether it was helping us choose dishes or checking in to make sure everything was perfect, their service was warm and sincere. We were visiting Mumbai from outside the city for just four days, and we ended up eating at Golden Chimney four out of five days — that says everything. When you find a place that combines amazing food with outstanding hospitality, you naturally want to return. Every time we came back, the quality was consistent and impressive.
The money we spent was absolutely worth it.
The portion sizes, the flavor, the cleanliness, and the service all reflect great value for the price.
It's rare to find a restaurant where both the food and the people leave such a lasting impression.
If you're in Mumbai and want authentic, flavorful food with heartfelt hospitality, Golden Chimney is a must-visit. We will definitely return the next time we are in the city.

featured_reviews.name: Debabrata Golder
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you are a seafood lover looking for an authentic and budget-friendly meal near Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CST), Sandeep Gomantak Hotel is an absolute must-visit.
Getting There & Parking
The restaurant is incredibly convenient if you are traveling by train, located just a short 5 to 7-minute walk from the CST station. I highly recommend that you go by walk only. Because it is situated in a bustling, crowded area, there is absolutely no parking available. Trying to find a spot for your vehicle nearby is a major problem and will only add unnecessary hassle to your meal, so walking is definitely the smartest option.
Ambiance & Service
Despite being a busy eatery, the management does a great job of maintaining the space. The dining area is kept very neat and clean, making for a comfortable environment to enjoy your meal. Additionally, the service is impressively fast. The staff is efficient and attentive, ensuring you get your food quickly even during peak lunch or dinner hours.
The Food
The star of the show here is undoubtedly the authentic Konkan-style cooking. The fish items are perfectly spiced, incredibly fresh, and exceptionally tasty. What makes it even better is that everything is well under budget, offering fantastic value for money without compromising on flavor. If you visit, you absolutely must try the crab—it is wonderfully prepared and easily one of the standout dishes on the menu.
Verdict
Overall, Sandeep Gomantak offers a fantastic, no-frills dining experience that hits all the right notes for coastal food cravings. Fast service, clean surroundings, and mouth-watering seafood make it a true hidden gem. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Yogen Sachdev
featured_reviews.review_text:
I finally revisited Maaslli – Saraswat and GSB Speciality last night for my annual catch-up with friends, and once again, it reminded me why this place is rightly awarded the best seafood restaurant in Mumbai.

We started off with their seafood soup, which was practically a treasure hunt in a bowl, packed with so many varieties of seafood that I stopped trying to count after a few spoonfuls. A rich, flavorful start that set the tone for the evening.

Next came the Bombil Fry, and let me say this: if you visit Maaslli and skip this, you’re missing the highlight of the menu. Perfectly crisp on the outside, melt-in-your-mouth inside, it was unanimously the table favorite.

The Prawns Ghee Roast, their signature dish, followed, aromatic, buttery, and spicy in all the right ways. You could taste the freshness of the prawns through the layers of ghee and masala.

I ordered the cucumber mint cooler as a palette cleanser, one of the best non-alcoholic drinks I’ve had. Truly impressed by the bar at this outlet

To round things off, we indulged in the Crab Gravy with Bhakri, a true coastal comfort combination. The gravy had that home-style depth of flavor that only comes from slow cooking and authentic spices.

Between the impeccable flavors, warm service, and the nostalgic coastal touch in every dish, Maaslli continues to set the gold standard for seafood in Mumbai. Can’t wait for next year’s reunion, though honestly, I might not wait that long to go back.

Special mention to the Owner of Maasli, Prasad Nayak who takes so much care and puts in the effort to keep the authentic heritage of GSB Food alive. Coming back for more!
Seafood lovers, you cant miss this one for sure!

featured_reviews.name: Sarthak Sahoo
featured_reviews.review_text: We dined in here for lunch and the restaurant was beautiful. The manager was polite and suggested great food to us. We had ordered Bombil Thali as well as Surmai Thali which was very tasty along with that we had Prawn ghee roast which was amazingly tasty and made us lick our fingers and we had to order extra Bhakri for that as well. Overall great lunch with great and tasty and amazing food and had a great experience overall. I would like to Thank the Manager of the restaurant and all the restaurants staffs for such beautiful hospitality and food.

featured_reviews.name: Yongmei Zhang
featured_reviews.review_text: Fish is very fresh, both curry and fry were done very well and tasty. Chicken was ok, the rice flour roti was a bit dry and not soft enough. Service was very good.

featured_reviews.name: Arun Hegden
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had incredible food here. The ambience was perfect. The service personnel were very welcoming. Anthony especially explained me well about the various thalis and accompaniments. I ordered a pomfret thali along with butter milk. The food was absolutely mouthwatering. Fish was fresh and very well marinated and cooked.
I just wished I could get a little veg accompaniment along though. Just to balance out the fiber.
The portion size was perfect.
Would highly recommend and visit again.

featured_reviews.name: NOSHIR KATRAK
featured_reviews.review_text:
Maaslli Restaurant & Bar, at Kemps Corner, Mumbai.
Basically a Sea food Restaurant, but also have other non veg dishes on their platter.
One cannot afford to miss the fried Bombil (Fresh, Fried Bombay Ducks).
They have a great Menu.
They do have various Thali dishes and other alcarte dishes.
It is just mouth watering and thus unable to put in words to describe the dishes.
One must enjoy the crab dishes and crab soup.
They also present you their fresh catch and you may select the fish if your choice, depending upon the weight the rate is fixed.
The atmosphere is damn cool and decent with fishes reflecting in the walls and partisans.
The curry, different types is served and we are asked to taste, then by adding coconut oil again to try. Thus if you are ordering any curry dish you can select your choice of curry.
The staff is very courteous and friendly.
The person, Mr. Anthony, accepting the order is very polite and well versed with the description of the dishes.
Service is quite fast and dishes are very tempting.
The complete crockery is if copper OR may be brass (not sure). But it is a real experience to have your food in such dish and even the fork and spoon.
The soup was something different from the normal ones which all must have experienced.
Crab soup, very tasty and hot enough and goes without saying very tasty.
Sweet dish of Modak and a sweetening dish made if milk and sprinkled with pista, woh! Lovely.
The dishes are well place and economically rated.
If you are in that area, do give a try and taste the tasty dishes, yes! Definitely one have a inclination and a taste for Sea Food.
The Bar is open and you have choices of hard drinks, Cocktails and even Mocktails.
A seperate Menu displaying the drinks is maintained.
Do visit, you will not regret nor your pockets will be pinched.
Enjoy the Sea Food and friendly service.

featured_reviews.name: Makarand Sainis
featured_reviews.review_text:
Excellent Seafood restaurant in Mumbai. A very old mangalorian style seafood restaurant which also offers other non veg and veg dishes.

Food quality is exceptional. Very tasty food with least spices. Portions are quite sufficient.

Must try Butter Garlic Prawns and Butter Garlic Crab here. Also, Pomfret, Surmai, Bombil (Bombay Duck), crabs, lobsters are very very good and very tasty.

Do not miss out chicken Makhani (Butter Chicken). One of the finest butter chicken I had in years.

Service is very quick, servers are very polite and helpful.

Seating capacity is less (26 tables, max 100 guests) and restaurant is always full. So, make sure you book table in advance before coming to Trishna for Lunch or dinner.

featured_reviews.name: Dan Liu
featured_reviews.review_text: I’m baffled by the popularity of this place. The garlic butter crab was decent, but that was about it. The biryani was lukewarm, the butter chicken tasted more like sweat than usual, and the Bombay duck was nothing special. Despite these shortcomings, the place is clearly popular, as you can feel the rush to seat the next customer. This place was highly recommended, but it didn’t live up to the hype.

featured_reviews.name: Anagha Surve
featured_reviews.review_text: Seafood lovers this is ‘The Best’ experience you will ever have. Lots of options in appetisers and the seafood is fresh and cooked to perfection. Tried their Singaporean Crab it was lip-smackingly good. Their pomfret and prawns dishes are also lovely. Quantity and portions are good.

featured_reviews.name: Shantanu Dey (Sandy)
featured_reviews.review_text: Without doubt one of the best seafood joints of Mumbai. We had their best selling ‘crab butter garlic’ which is always awesome. This time we also tried the Hyderabadi rawas tikka suggested by our steward. With subtle tastes of masala this was great too! Didn’t have space for any dessert. Prices are on the higher side and so is the experience.

featured_reviews.name: rushda moulvi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Trishna truly lives up to its reputation. In my opinion, it’s one of the best seafood restaurants in Mumbai.

The prawn ghee roast is exceptional. Even though I’m not usually a big fish lover, their Schezwan fish and biryani are absolutely delicious. The seafood is extremely fresh with no smell at all.

Also love their butter naan and cheese naan. A special mention to the staff extremely professional, friendly, and attentive.A must-visit for anyone coming to Mumbai

featured_reviews.name: Shreyas Nair
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely Amazing Seafood, Really nice food but quite pricey. Must visit if you’re in the area and want to have some seafood. We visited for dinner and spent 2.5k per head.
Here are our recommendations:
Tiger butter garlic prawn 10/10 MUST HAVE
Pomphret ghee roast - 9/10 can try the prawn ghee roast as well
Neer dosa - really good
Appam - this was a miss, not as good as Kerala Appam
Coorg promphet curry - A really nice coriander based curry to have with rice or bread

featured_reviews.name: Amiit k Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had an amazing meal at Mao Family Restaurant–Best family Restaurant Kalbadevi-Best North Indian,Mughlai,Chinese,Arabian,Seafood Restaurant Kalbadevi! 😍

The Paneer Schezwan Khepsa Rice was packed with flavor, perfectly spicy, and loaded with delicious paneer pieces. The Manchurian Chatpata was crispy, tangy, and a perfect starter. The highlight was definitely the Hungama Khepsa Rice — huge portion size, rich taste, and enough to satisfy the whole group. Every bite was flavorful and satisfying.

Great food quality, generous portions, and excellent value for money. A must-visit place for Khepsa lovers in Mumbai! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

featured_reviews.name: Samruddhi Hambire
featured_reviews.review_text: Visited Mao Family Restaurant for lunch and tried the Hungama Kepsa (half) — good portion size and flavorful, definitely worth it. The Chicken Tandoori was outstanding; juicy, well-marinated, and something I would surely recommend to any non-vegetarian.However, the vegetarian menu was a huge disappointment. The Paneer Kepsa tasted more like a Chinese-style gravy than authentic Kepsa, and the Paneer Crispy was neither crispy nor made from real paneer — it was clearly synthetic. At ₹265, the quantity and quality of paneer were unacceptable.In short, this place is a delight for non-vegetarians but a nightmare for vegetarians.

featured_reviews.name: Sushant Kadam
featured_reviews.review_text: Service was quick. Their speciality kepsa even half is enough for 3-4 people. The waiter suggested us hungama kepsa as their most popular kepsa. It was worth the price. Had 3 types of starters inside kepsa. Only thing is table dining arrangement is not much spacious and you need to adjust accordingly.

featured_reviews.name: srinivas goud
featured_reviews.review_text:
Yummiest food I have ever had in Mumbai.. ordered Schezwan chicken fried rice..
. Taste is best. Quantity and quality both are good.. affordable compared to other restaurants. Supportive staff .. would definitely visit again..

featured_reviews.name: Strengers Fights
featured_reviews.review_text: The food quality at Mao Restaurant is very poor. The rice is often undercooked and completely tasteless. The overall quality of the food is extremely disappointing. Even the service is not proper, and the plates and bowls do not seem properly cleaned. I would strongly advise people to avoid eating here.

featured_reviews.name: bhavika jethwa
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Mao Restaurant and had an incredible dining experience! I ordered the Chicken Noorani Kabab and Chicken Tikka Mini Kepsa, and I must say, the kababs were absolutely delicious. They had a delightful tandoori coating, and the filling was made of perfectly spiced seekh chicken. The spice level was just right—medium spicy, which added to the overall flavor without overwhelming the palate.

What made it even more special was that it was served on a sizzling plate, enhancing the presentation and aroma. The Chicken Tikka Mini Kepsa was a unique addition to the menu, and being the first place to serve it definitely earned them some extra points. The taste was simply amazing, and each bite was a burst of flavor.

I would highly recommend Mao Restaurant to anyone looking for a great meal. The combination of delicious food, unique offerings, and excellent presentation makes it a must-visit spot. Can't wait to go back and try more dishes!

Respected Sir/Madam,

I recently ordered food from your restaurant through a delivery service. I ordered a half plate of Chilly Kepsa, but my experience was very disappointing.

The boiled egg in the dish had a very bad smell, which made the food inedible. This clearly indicates that the food was not fresh and raises serious concerns about hygiene and quality.

I request you to please look into this matter seriously and ensure that proper quality checks are done before sending food for delivery.

I hope you will take necessary action so that such issues do not happen again.

Thank you.

Yours sincerely,
Himanshu Gupta

featured_reviews.name: Abhilasha Akhade
featured_reviews.review_text:
I would never give the review or recommend this place to any one, On 17/04/2026, my friends and I visited the restaurant for dinner. After finishing our meal, we stepped outside and were waiting for a cab when one of my friends suddenly collapsed due to low blood pressure and fainted right outside your restaurant.

In that moment of urgency, I approached your staff requesting a small amount of sugar to help revive her. However, I was shocked by their response—they bluntly said they do not keep sugar. What was even more surprising was that at the same time, sugar was clearly available in the mukhwas kept there.

It was a matter of basic human kindness, and such a small help could have made a big difference in that situation. Unfortunately, the staff showed complete lack of empathy and humanity.

This is particularly disappointing because Kalbadevi has always been a place we frequently visit for lunch and dinner. Experiencing such insensitive behavior from your team was unexpected and unacceptable.

I do have a video of the incident, I will upload it soon. I will Raise a complaint too.
